newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico ruling party steps up attacks on opposition.
newsitem.headline: Mexico ruling party steps up attacks on opposition.

text.p: The head of Mexico's ruling party has unleashed a new attack on the two major opposition parties, warning of a potential for "dictatorship" or "fascism" if the right wing or the left come to power.

Humberto Roque Villanueva, president of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) that has ruled for 67 years, ratcheted up the intensity of the battle against the conservative National Action Party (PAN) and leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) on Sunday.
Watershed congressional elections are set for July 6.

"We don't like ideological extremes because in the long run ... the right starts out as likeable but ends up as fascist, and the left starts out apparently social but ends up in dictatorship," Roque told a labour confederation.
Roque is continuing the line of his predecessor, Santiago Ontate Labourde, who characterised the PRI as the centrist option between two extremes. Onate was dismissed in December.

The PAN is a party of the free market and a moral social policy that has made a steady series of electoral gains since winning the first opposition governorship in 1989. The PRD, which favours government intervenion to aid the poor, is a relative newcomer that fared well in local elections in 1996.
